newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom shares up in grey market.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom shares up in grey market.

text.p: Shares in soon-to-be-floated German telecoms monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG traded 13.3 percent above the higher end of the initial price range put at 25-30 marks in the "grey market" on Friday, dealers said.

The grey market refers to the market provided by brokers prior to a formal offering which is not subject to official controls. Shares are sold ahead of the offering and the contracts are honoured when the IPO officially takes place.

"Volumes are limited at the moment, because the majority of the banks and their subsidiaries are restricted from trading as they form part of the syndicate behind the flotation," a trader with Frankfurt brokers Ballmaier & Schulz said.

The first tranche of Deutsche Telekom is due to be sold off on November 18 in what will be Europe's biggest-ever flotation. Telekom will float 500 million shares as part of the global flotation and banks have the option to exercise a "greenshoe", or over-allotment, offering of 75 million additional shares.
A trader at the Uto Baader brokerage in Munich said: "We had very good volumes in the grey market when trade began at the start of the week."

"However, the fact that syndicate-members are restricted from dealing in Deutsche Telekom on the grey market scared people off. This means that our main trading partners have been foreign clients," the Baader trader said.
Ballmaier and Schulz said the share had been trading between 33 marks and 33.50 marks earlier in the day, but by the end of the day the price had risen to between 33.90 marks and 34.20 marks.
"We're seeing interest between 33.90 marks and 34.90 marks -- people are definitely interested at the 34-mark level," the Baader trader said.

Hamburg dealers Saunders & Zellweger GmbH was quoting a price of between 33.15 marks and 33.35 marks, while Frankfurt's Kling & Jelko brokerage was quoting a range of between 33.70 marks and 34.20 marks.
Dealers said that trade on the grey market is a useful guideline and that they pay attention to the share price as a price guide.

Deutsche Telekom said earlier in the week that the price range for its shares in the IPO next month would be between 25 and 30 marks. The final price for the share issue will be set in the weekend of November 16-19.

In a separate development, DB Capital Markets issued 1.5 million American-style call and put warrants, in marks, in three equal tranches, on Deutsche Telekom AG, lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
